content.title: About
content.content: A fruit smoothie with whole fruit, dairy, and added protein is a nutrient‑dense beverage that blends the natural sweetness of ripe fruit, the creamy texture of milk, and an extra protein boost to support muscle recovery and satiety.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole‑fruit blends retain fiber, vitamins, and minerals that are lost when using only fruit purées.
Dairy adds calcium and vitamin D, contributing to bone health.
Protein from whey or plant isolates improves the amino‑acid profile of the drink.
Athletes often use fruit smoothies as a quick post‑workout recovery shake.
Varying the fruit mix lets you switch from tropical to berry‑focused flavors.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and antioxidants
items.content: Fruits provide vitamin C, vitamin A, and polyphenols that support immunity and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Added protein supplies essential amino acids for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Dairy ingredients help strengthen bones and teeth.

items.title: Fiber for digestion
items.content: Whole fruit retains dietary fiber, promoting healthy gut function.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: The combination of natural fruit sugars and slower‑digesting carbs provides lasting fullness and energy.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with these conditions should use plant‑based milk alternatives.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Multiple sweet fruits can raise the drink’s glycemic index; diabetics should monitor portion size.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of fruit and protein may cause bloating in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Protein and dairy increase calories; consider the portion within your daily energy budget.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Consume the smoothie immediately after blending to preserve vitamin freshness. It works well as a breakfast, post‑workout snack, or light dinner. Add ice for extra refreshment or swap dairy for a plant‑based milk if a lactose‑free option is needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared smoothie in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, portion and freeze; thaw in the fridge before drinking and give it a quick shake.
